reviews.text:
These guys are the real deal! Our dog was becoming unwalkable - dragging us everywhere on the lead, lunging, barking and going crazy at other dogs. YCA's promise that we would be calmly sat in the pub with other reactive dogs by the end of the was true, we did exactly that.

Best money we have ever spent, we have a brand new dog... unrecognisable from before we attended the bootcamp. We also now have the tools, knowledge and more importantly ability to contact them for more advice if we ever have any other specific issues. The facilities at YCA are great, lots of fields nearby for walks to test out the training. The staff are brilliant - really friendly and know their stuff. Highly recommended!

It’s rare to encounter a business where the staff are as enthusiastic about the service as the customer who needs it. This is true for YCA for one simple reason, they are all dog owners, rescuers, fosterers, trainers and above all dog lovers. This is clear from the moment you step in to the great facilities they run (in our case) at their Leeds site.
There is a saying: ‘love what you do and you’ll never work a day in your life’. This seems to ring true for all the staff at YCA.
Their service transcends common terms such as ‘excellent’ because it contains care… which you can’t put a price on.

YCA was recommended to us by a stranger who is now a friend. We commented on how well behaved their dog was and they said it was all down to the boot camp at YCA.
The proof to us was there and although we had to have a serious think about it because of cost, I can now say that it was worth every single penny. Our dog was very reactive to other dogs, walks were always in quiet areas avoiding dogs, cafes were a no no, a drink at a pub was always outside in a far corner of the beer garden and if we had food it was something which could be eaten with one hand as the other was hanging on to the dog. I couldn’t believe that in 5 days we would be in cafes and pubs (eating with a knife AND fork) with other dogs and she would be off lead on walks (she would never be off lead before and we were always on edge)
We have now had a whole new world opened up to us, we are all much more relaxed. My husband didn’t attend the camp and has been blown away by the change. We are only on the third day after boot camp but the results so far are amazing.
All the staff at YCA are knowledgeable and genuinely caring and we can’t thank them enough. 😊

I attended Yorkshire Canine Academy Boot Camp with my two dogs, and I’m absolutely thrilled with the progress we’ve made.

Prior to attending one of my dogs was extremely reactive towards other dogs, The other was prey driven and I was one of those who would travel miles each day to walk in quiet places where the chances of any issues arising were slim.

At the start of the week, I set myself a goal: to be able to take my dogs across to the playing field opposite my house and walk around the lakes without any issues. Something that I have not been able to do for fear of generating a negative reputation; However, today I am delighted to say that I’ve now achieved exactly that walk With no issues.

Both dogs were brilliant. We encountered other dogs in a variety of situations, including several off lead around us, and I was amazed by how calmly my two behaved. Most rewarding of all was seeing one of my dogs recognise a potentially difficult situation and choose to move away himself. That really was a fantastic moment.

I also incorporated the post boot camp e-collar training into our loose-lead walking, following the video guidance, and saw results within just two minutes! The difference this training has made to our walks has been incredible, and I’m excited to continue building on what we’ve learned.

The boot camp has given me greater confidence, practical techniques to work with and, most importantly, the opportunity to enjoy walking my dogs with far less stress. For me, the results speak for themselves, and I’m genuinely delighted with what we’ve achieved.

There are a few aspects of the overall organisation and communication that could be improved to make the experience even better, but these do not take away from the progress we have made through the training.

Thank you to Yorkshire Canine Academy for helping us take such a positive step forward. I’m thrilled with the outcome and would encourage anyone considering the boot camp to look at what it could help them achieve with their own dogs. Yes, it is a significant investment but it is worth every penny, and I’m glad I did not hesitate.

So as most of you reading this and not believing that your dog can be 'fixed' Mabel our 4 year old dachshund was a nightmare. We had been asked to leave pubs and socialising sessions. Barking lunging at people and she had biten both of us. The idea of a walk at the weekend was just get it done early and get on with my day.

So we booked on the 5 day boot camp. Im not lying when I say this Mabel is so much calmer, friendly with dogs most importantly she actually enjoys her walks.

The staff at YCA are so helpful and are always willing to answer any concerns. The great thing about it for us is the fact that if anythings creeps back after the boot camp YCA are always there to help and invite you down to go over things you are struggling with.

Took my very dog and somewhat people rective dog to them for their Bootcamp training .... for a dog that was becoming unmanageable to being able to sit in a pub with my dog by my side AND to be able let her have off lead walks in a public park was a miracle for us.... plus loads of back up if/when needed ..... price seems expensive but worth every penny when it worked .. money back if they do not

Just got back from our bootcamp week. As a human who owns a German wirehaired pointer pup, I have come away with a completely different mindset and approach.

All the trainers are lovely but it's not about making us feel comfortable, it's about making sure our dogs are fulfilled and happy... which can  sometimes make us feel uncomfortable! But that is where the growth happens.

I've a knackered pup tonight wanting to have clear, calm commands. Because that's what they've been used to this week. So my job moving forward is to be firm, consistent and calm. Tools and all the gear round their neck at first was a lot and my dog scratted and scratched. But know now this has been the reset for him to feel safe and yet also be the crazy rampunctious and inquisitive dog he is, without the reactivity and negative reactions we both hate.

I can't thank the staff enough, there's been no judgement (I mean he was called a lot of names he hadn't heard before), but what they did so consistently was met a nervous mam dog with kindness and direction.

This has given me the focus I needed, not just for me, but to show my children how to give a dog their best life.

Thank you ❤️

Absolute best decision and best investment I’ve ever made. If you’re in any doubt about whether or not to choose YCA or whether you can justify spending the money I can wholeheartedly reassure you it will be the best thing you could do for your dog. It will open up the world to you and improve your dogs life massively!  We can all be guilty of spending money on things that we could live without….that holiday, new phone, new car etc and if you just miss one holiday and do this you won’t regret it. The instructors are so knowledgeable, the support and care from all the staff is incredible. I literally cannot recommend YCA highly enough. If you’re in any doubt JUST DO IT!! Thank you so much YCA

Not sure where to start with this.. As most dog reactive owners, I was of course slightly sceptical that YCA would be able to me; not because of their skills/knowledge, i just wasn't sure my dog (Pepper) was fixable due to her being scared of everything.

How wrong i was - the training was absolutely fantastic. It's not just about training dogs, it's also training us so we know how to pay/reward, correct, notice things, what is and isn't allowed and so on.

The team were amazing - in particular to shout out Lee, Toni and Ian (and Alex), but they immediately put you at ease, and can answer every single question you throw at them, with reasons why backing up the answers.

I didn't believe i'd be sat in a pub by the end of the week - but i was. Pepper wasn't comfortable still, but she was calm, and reacted amazingly to the environment, considering it's one she has never, ever been in before.

And, Pepper also won me a prize for 'most improved dog', and i've not had the hoodie off since.

I honestly can't recommend YCA enough, and the Bootcamp. It's a super well structured and well organised week, and all your issues/questions are addressed, even personal goals for each client (i.e. window/car barking, livestock reactivity, leash walking etc etc).

I'm genuinely sad to be back at home this week - i wish I could take Pepper everyday and work with the team, go on the group walks etc

Massive thanks to the team for changing my life for the better - i've gone from dreading walking the dogs, to actually looking forward to it now, and that has massively improved my life and mental health already!

10/10 would recommend to anyone

It’s been one week and one day since Hedgehog (our extremely reactive Lurcher) graduated from YCA. I was very sceptical when booking and even on first two days days of Bootcamp. What I can now is “WOW”, I won’t say he’s a different dog but me and my husband have been out on walks, a trip to the pub and today was his biggest achievement so far. We went to Stretford Makers Market which was very very busy with so so many dogs which he handled like a champ. When we adopted Hedgehog last year we didn’t think something like this would be possible so I want to say a massive and heartfelt thank you to all the team at YCA.

The results from the Boot camp were way better than we even hoped. Before training we couldn’t walk Bear down the road. He’d react to any large dog, child, jogger, bike, scooter, motorbike etc. etc. Walking him was relentlessly stressful and it impacted our lives in so many ways.
By the end of the week we walked down a canal path past bikes, dogs, joggers and had lunch in the pub with 14 other ‘reactive’ dogs. After a week home he’s just as good. It has really changed our (and Bear’s) lives.

I don’t know where to start!!

We have just returned from Bootcamp with our 2 German Shepherds. One of them had already bitten 2 people and they were both reactive to other dogs

I never thought that after a mere 5 days, my dogs would be safely off lead, walking with other dogs nearby and sitting in a pub without barking

If you have any doubts about whether this will work, don’t!  The staff are all so friendly, knowledgeable and helpful. They work incredibly hard to make sure that you get as much as you want and need out of their expertise. Nothing is too much trouble!

Before I came I didn’t believe that anything could be done for our dogs, especially not in 5 days. I’d read the reviews but didn’t believe them. How wrong was I?  I know people often say if it looks too good to be true, then it probably is. However as far as Yorkshire Canine Academy is concerned, it most certainly isn’t!!!

If you have a high drive reactive dog YCA will get you there to a much better relationship and life with your dog! I am in the states and was hesitant to do their online program, but they held my hand every step of the way and were incredibly patient as I developed my knowledge and skills, asked a million questions, and worked through all of my own fears and anxieties. I did work my butt off for a few months, but a year later I am continuing to reap the rewards and am completely relaxed and confident in 99% of situations and still growing. My dog went from being reactive, sensitive, nervy, and unreliable to being locked in on me with rock solid recall. She is so much happier, calmer, and more confident. She now has full freedom on her ecollar to roam, sniff, and track to her heart's content (beagle/husky mix). I trust her almost completely and can instantly call her off chasing a deer, critters, another dog, anything we have encountered so far with no ecollar stim at all! Thank-you YCA! Please franchise in the USA!

YCA changed my dog's life and mine from the other side of the world. If you don't live near one of their locations, they have a fully online program so you can still work with these exceptional trainers.

Every other trainer told me my Jack Russell Chihuahua mix Winnie was always going to bark at everyone and everything and the only solutions they could give for her reactivity were to strictly manage her at all times. The idea of ever having a JRT mix off-leash was dismissed by everyone I spoke to as impossible.

Cut to 3 weeks post-Training With Instinct and Winnie gets off-leash time to run around everyday. She has a completely reliable recall and can heel off-leash. My friends are begging me to train their dogs. If it sounds too good to be true, just look at my before and after videos taken just 6 weeks apart.

I've had many dogs that were decently well behaved, but this is on another level and I can't imagine ever going back. It was the best money I've maybe ever spent. Not only do I have a dog I can take anywhere, but I've also developed handling skills I'll have for the rest of my life.

I can't thank everyone at YCA enough. If your dog is at all reactive, this is the only place to go. They will solve all your problems and more.

I would recommend YCA wholeheartedly. This is not just about addressing reactivity, but giving us humans the tools and skills to move forward with our dogs. All the trainers are brilliant. Amazing with the dogs, but also good with us humans. Their patient and ready to answer any and all of your questions. Their calmness helps you to move forward with difficult situations and doing this in real life situations. I can't wait to get out with my dog and have full and fun life with him.
Thank you YCA

Ragnar, our Long-haired German Shepherd, had always been very reactive towards dogs, pulling against his slip lead, quite happy to choke himself to get to another dog, at times showing aggression with hackles up, a nightmare on walks and definitely a no-go when it comes to taking him into bars or cafes, always having to scout ahead to check for other dogs.
And then YCA Bootcamp...
Thoughts prior to booking? Will it work? All previous training methods never. Some training methods work in the very short term but 24 hours later back to the same reactivity. Also, to be honest, sounded expensive, but with the reassurance of money back if it didn't work - fair enough - we booked in.
Bootcamp was great and straight away worth the money, great facilities, plenty YCA trainers at hand to answer all questions - not quite one to one dog to YCA Trainer ratio but at times it felt like it was. And the point of it was that they were there to train us how to train our dog. Which they did very well - very informative, with the training method (and phycology behind it) explained very well. Training was tailored to suit our dog. Equipment supplied fantastic.
We deliberately left it a few weeks before leaving a review just to be sure the methods taught worked - they do! Weekend after the Bootcamp we were staying in a dog friendly hotel sitting having dinner with Ragnar lying at our feet. Off lead walks round our local Golf course with the reassurance that the recall will work. Taking trips through to village markets and walking with Ragnar - other dogs kicking off barking at him and Ragnar just looks at them as if to say 'what's your problem?' then looks up at us and we walk on by.. amazing!!!
The training will of course continue, never stops I guess, but the promise of 100% turnaround of Ragnar's reactivity in 5 day Bootcamp was real.
Excellent so far, currently on day 3 and me and my GSD have learnt a lot 😁

Was skeptical about this after been to a previous trainer, but we're left speechless after 5 days hugo our 18month old cane corso was asleep in the pub while we ate !!! With plenty of other dogs and people around.

Hugo was reactive to other dogs and passers by. Walking him just wasn't enjoyable at all heading out scanning the street the path ahead just looking for triggers, that another trainer had basically told us to avoid ie ( crossing the road, switching hugo to different sides and changing direction ).

Fast forward 5 days and hes walking nicely on a loose lead no pulling and no reacting. Carnt thank the amazing team at yca enough for helping him and also kicking my ass when I wasn't firm enough with him. 🤣

Been a good boy must be hard work here he his fast asleep !!!

Well we were off to Hever Castle for the weekend but my birthday plans were changed to spend time at YCA instead. And booking in for 2 one day courses over the weekend worked out to be an excellent decision!
After a brilliant bootcamp back in February, we were loving life with Codie, our 2 year old GSD as we could now enjoy relaxed, social walks and visits to pubs etc. This was all impossible as well as a huge strain before the Feb.bootcamp because he was so excitable and strong. Now we all love his fulfilled life off lead and able to pass dogs happily.
So why did we go back? Firstly, we loved the instructors and got so much from the bootcamp we wanted to just do more with them. And there were a couple of things that niggled which we wanted to address with YCA direction so Codie got clear messages.
No matter how well things might seem to be going, we can easily slip into bad or lazy habits and consistency between Tim and myself was beginning to deteriorate.
Anyway, long story short .... it happened that we got amazing one to one time, first with Kirkey then with Elisha. They were so helpful  and I can't describe how much we learnt, appreciated and enjoyed that time. The following day we were in a small group working on re-socialisation with Owain and Lee - who both gave us so much close support and time to get us working clearly and effectively with Codie. We continue to practise their instructions (which as ever make so much sense) and hope Owain will be pleased that we've found a dog group and Codie is a perfect gent. Also we will get our heel work video to Lee very soon! All I can say is, it is invaluable to revisit past learning - we have come away with loads more than we could have imagined.
Huge buckets of thanks again to YCA and we'll be up your way again when we can!

We went to Bootcamp late August so we are now about one month on.

Our lab/collie cross became dog reactive at about one year old. After three years of counter conditioning and positive reinforcement, we made great progress but we'd hit a ceiling. Having struggled to see any dog without reacting, he could be around dogs and pass most dogs without incident, but he was always at high arousal and struggled with head on passes and any dogs coming too close. He had particular challenges with GSDs, other large breeds, or dogs that stared at him.

The Mon and Tues of Bootcamp builds the base that helps you better communicate with your dog. This adds to the pre-work in building food and play drive, and conditioning a strong 'yes' terminal marker. The team then helped us condition a solid negative marker. This really moved the needle for us, as for the first time we were able to interrupt his unwanted behaviour successfully, and communicate that it wasn't acceptable or necessary. E-collar was layered on his recall (which was always very strong), so that is now completely bombproof.

The Weds-Fri of the week, we took it off-site and practiced in the real world. These are great experiences. Our first off-site venture, we turned a corner in the face of an off-lead GSD that was not with the group. Our dog sniffed him and carried on. This would have been lunges with teeth just a few days before.

Post-Bootcamp, his threshold is way higher. He has had a couple of small reactions - two to dogs reacting to him first, one very rude dog that ran straight into his face, one on our street (which trainers said would be the most challenging area). All were proportionate, but the difference now is we know exactly what to do and each repetition of the 'bad' protocol makes a future reaction less likely. The larger caveat on this is we are putting him in way more challenging situations that we would previously, such as walking on the canal we had avoided for a long time due to the lack of options to create space. We are now confident to take him anywhere, and his world is far bigger because we're confident in ourselves and the tools provided.

We've also attended the Saturday socialisation sessions and have done a further Mastery day class just to reinforce new behaviours around more dogs. These are a great resource to top up your training.

Many thanks to Owain, Mel, Alex, Lee, Elisha, Kirky, and Toni - everyone we worked with at YCA was super supportive throughout and told us exactly what we needed to do in every situtaion. Highly recommended to anyone struggling with a reactive dog. Worth the money 5 times over.

We’ve just finished our 5 day bootcamp with YCA, and I honestly can’t recommend them enough.

Obi was reactive to other dogs, and after trying multiple local trainers with very little success, we were starting to feel completely at a dead end. I’ll admit, I had reservations about the use of e-collars and more so prong collars, but I went in with an open mind and I’m so glad I did!!

Each member of the YCA team take the time to educate you on both the theory and practical reasons behind the tools and methods they use, while making sure you understand how to use them safely and correctly. They’re all incredibly friendly and supportive, but most importantly, they genuinely have the dogs best interests at heart. They make sure you’re doing the right thing, at the right time, for the right reasons.

The cost can seem like a lot initially, but seeing the difference in Obi already, alongside the difference in me as an owner and the knowledge and confidence I now have is genuinely priceless.

We still have work to do in maintaining this at home, but we finally feel like we have the tools and understanding to help Obi moving forward. I honestly don’t believe anyone would ever regret choosing YCA! ❤️🐾

We graduated Bootcamp yesterday and I honestly can’t believe the difference in our dog.

We went into the week nervous about what to expect. We were unsure about some of the training tools, including e-collars, but decided to go with an open mind because everything else we had tried had failed. Our goal was actually quite simple: we wanted a happier, more confident dog who could relax around other dogs and enjoy a walk without constantly scanning his surroundings and becoming anxious.

We didn’t even dare imagine we might one day have him safely off lead around other dogs.

I’ll admit, during the first couple of days I wondered how we were possibly going to see a significant change. There’s a lot of theory, foundation work and some waiting around watching others, and at first it can feel like you aren’t doing enough hands-on training with your dog.

Then day three arrives.

You get out into the real world and suddenly everything from those first two days starts clicking into place. You realise why those foundations were so important.

By days four and five, we had a completely different dog.

We went from having a dog who couldn’t be walked outside without an uncontrollable and dangerous reaction to another dog (near or far), to a dog who loose-lead walks and is an absolute pleasure to take out.

We walked around the lake at Roundhay Park past dogs in close proximity with ZERO reaction. He settled and relaxed in a pub with another dog lying next to him. And, unbelievably, the week culminated with him enjoying complete freedom off lead with around other dogs surrounding him.

He now has a fantastic recall too, which feels like an incredible bonus because we genuinely never went to bootcamp expecting that.

We went to Yorkshire Canine Academy simply hoping they could improve his dog reactivity enough for us to enjoy walking him. What we came away with was so much more and, most importantly, so much more freedom and enjoyment for him.

I can’t thank every single member of the team enough for their care, attention and patience. These guys clearly love dogs deeply. You see it not just in the training, but in the way they interact with the dogs and bring their own dogs to work with them.

If you’re nervous because of things you’ve heard about some of the training tools they use, I’d say go and see it for yourself with an open mind. From our experience, the tools are used minimally and as part of a much bigger training approach.

For us, the result has been a dog with more freedom, more confidence and a family who can finally confidently enjoy taking him out.

We honestly never thought we’d get here. 💛🐾

Our German shepherd has always been fairly reactive, we thought we were getting somewhere but he started to become aggressive towards dogs in particular but then this carried on to people, and it was getting worse. We had been following YCA and watching the videos of the changes in the boot camp. I have to admit we were somewhat sceptical it was a big statement they make. However we had got to the stage were we were not walking our dog at busy times, dreading meeting other dogs and then just worried about passing people. So we took the plunge. What could we loose if it worked, fantastic, if it didn’t at least we tried to do something. Even after day two I was still sceptical, some good guidance but off lead I couldn’t see that happening.
We have finished today where our German Shepherd was off lead with others all around, we did have lunch in a pub and it was fine and can see us continuing to do it.
The training team are extremely knowledgeable and down to earth, Tailor the training to each dogs specific needs. I now have a dog I am confident I can take out and control on/off the lead. Still work to do to ensure he stays there, but 100% well worth a week of your time if you want to enjoy your dog
Thanks YCA

Our dog charlie was a nightmare which has impacted our lives as we couldnt take him in public places or meet other dogs and people on walks as he would be so aggresive towards other dogs, cyclists, cars and some people. We discovered this after seeing some of the results and we signed up. Rhe guys at YCA have been fantastic and worked with us to train charlie to be a sociable dog. In just 5 days with them at boot camp has made an absolute difference to our lives and charlies allowing us to go into public places with our dog without a scene and be with other dogs.as the teaching they give really works. Thank you YCA you have changed our lives

I did boot camp with Clemmie. The change in both of us in 5 days is astonishing. We were lucky to have great people and dogs in the group and consistent excellent training from the staff. Your method works and we will continue to work with it. This makes a massive difference to Clemmie’s quality of life and by extension ours. Cannot offer any more praise than that!

We have just finished bootcamp and have nothing but praise for the YCA team.

Our Romanian rescue had serious reactivity issues to dogs, people approaching him (or us), runners, cars, bikes and pretty much anything else you could think of.

It soon became apparent that he wasn't going to fit into the usual training pattern with everyone else as he was having serious meltdowns and needed a bit of 1:1 work with the trainers.

By the end of day 2 after trying to annihilate them all single pawedly, he was chilling out in the meeting room almost fast asleep with seven of them.

Day 3 he was allowed back into the fold and by the end of the week he achieved the heretofore impossible feat of chilling out in a pub without even wearing a muzzle, something we'd not managed since he was a puppy.

He's only been out for one day in the real world so early days to see if we are following the plan well enough by ourselves but we have the ongoing lifetime support of the YCS team and will take him back to the Saturday meetings on a regular basis to help us all keep those skills honed.

However, we took him to Fountains Abbey today and he walked straight past lots of dogs with no incidents and queued with us for some lunch and settled at the table so we could eat our lunch with no stress.

All the trainers really carefully watched what he (and we) were doing  and gave us detailed feedback and coaching and all really seemed to care about the dogs and our progress. Thanks guys, we really appreciate all of you and your caring.

It was a lot of money for us but as long as we keep up the training it will have completely changed our lives for the better so well worth it.

We will report back again with our progress.

Had an extremely nervous & reactive dog prior going to YCA whom we were hoping that we could be worked on to deal with her reactivity. From the very start we found YCA to be friendly, professional and helpful. We had lots of communication prior to going, with helpful stuff to do to help prepare both Molly and ourselves. Whilst undergoing onsite training we found it to be very instructive. I was very nervous myself and when they said that we would have Molly walking with other dogs off lead and go and sit in a pub with all the others and have lunch along with the dogs I just did not believe. At all times we either worked with our dogs or whilst they were having a rest we were watching / listening & learningt whilst the others in our group did there stuff. By day 4 Molly was indeed walking with other dogs in a calm and controlled manner and walking in a park OFF LEAD. I cannot rate these guys high enough. The after care service is ongoing now with communication and visits when we want to do "top up" stuff or discuss any isses or problems or concerns that may occur. I would say to anybody who is hesitating - DON'T - it is the best thing you will EVER do for both yourself and you dog

After watching YouTube videos from YCA we realised we needed help with our young Jack Russell.  Always pulling, annoying other dogs and not listening when on walks. It was impossible to visit a cafe or pub as she barked and wouldn't sit still. 5 days of bootcamp at YCA and what a difference.  Walks past dogs nicely,  running happily off lead. We are now able to enjoy a coffee or a beer with May laying quietly. Thanks to all the team for making this happen.

It's changed my dogs life, the expense was a  big issue to accept but now looking back its worth the investment. The charges in him haven't come all at once but he's gradually developed over the last four months lowering his reactivity and his recall were the initial changes, his confidence has grown and positive changes in him have followed.

Great practical week of training and setting up e collar and prong collars.
Ongoing support and hints and tips available.
Socialisation classes afterwards are a godsend, and keep the handler in check aswell so no missed corrections.
The freedom this has given Ralph and us is amazing. He has the best quality of life with almost permanent off lead walks. He is also controlled on lead and not pulling our arms off.
Life changing. Worth the money 10 times over. Rocco is a changed dog and when we do have the odd blip I know how to handle it thanks to all the trainers at YCA 🙏

Casey and I attended boot camp this week as a final last ditch attempt at sorting this 7 year old boy’s reactivity, and the change in a week is remarkable. I’d tried all the usual training before, the 1:1, obedience stuff and one trainer was even visibly annoyed by how much Casey barked during an assessment session. I found YCA after some research online and going for an assessment with Elisha was one of the best decisions I’ve ever made for him.

Casey wasn’t reactive as you’d typically expect; no aggression really towards dogs, no dislike of people, no lunging, no running off (because he had never been off lead before!). Casey would become so overstimulated by the world and bark at everything, for the sake of barking sometimes, and there was nothing stopping him. He’d jump up, he wouldn’t settle, he was constantly reacting to his surroundings. We’d been asked to leave public places, beer gardens, and my family and friends did not enjoy being around him, he was putting a wedge in my relationship because of his behaviour at home. Fast forward a week on YCA’s boot camp and for the first time in his life, he has been off lead in public parks with impeccable recall, his barking is non existent, he does not pull on his lead, and we sat in a pub and had lunch stress free for the first time.

I would recommend this boot camp to anybody, but please also understand this is hard work for you too and it totally relies on you being committed and putting in the effort. Boot camp is not a quick fix, you will be tired, you will be frustrated, you will be expected to want to change your dog’s behaviour. Please make sure you do the pre-training work which was absolutely vital for Casey in getting the results we did. Take it seriously, be strict with yourself and put in the effort. It is no secret that YCA use tools, including E collars, and I’d advise you to do your own research. You’ll read the horror stories online, the unwavering criticism of such tools, but the use of these tools correctly and ethically have changed mine and my dog’s life.

To everyone at YCA- thank you. Your work with Casey this week has started the transformation of my dog and I can’t wait to see what’s to come in the future.

We have just completed the bootcamp with our two dogs Ronnie 6 (French Bulldog) and Betsy 4 (English Mastiff).

Its hard to put into words how doing this course is actually going to change your life.

Ronnie our Frenchie was really reactive with other dogs..he was completely frustrated and in doing so he would literally scream! It was beyond embarrassing - our walks became very schedule to quite only locations and avoiding other dogs - it really made our lifes difficult.

After day 3 Ronnie was walking around a field with other reactive dogs and by day 4 he was off lead coming back to me beautifully - i cried it was the best feeling seeing him free and happy!

We travelled 3 and half hours and it was completely worth the time, dedication and money.

Betsy our English mastiff is 11 stone and when she goes she goes large!

Her guarding was out of control with the van and it got resolved so easily we couldn't believe it!

Her recall is spot on and she now has a clear understanding of yes and no.

We have just completed our first walk back at home and we are so excited to show off our new skills and for everyone to see our well behaved happy dogs.

BIG THANKS to Toni, Owain, Alex, Lee, Mel  Fred's and young lad with Sheila and the lovely lady on reception!

We rescued our 2 year old Golden Retriever, Kennedy, last November, and she was extremely reactive to other dogs. She would lunge and bark at the sight of a dog, and could completely lose it even when a dog was a football field away. We were doing 4 AM and 9 PM walks just to avoid other dogs, and we were emotionally exhausted.

We found Jacob's training videos on YouTube and downloaded the Behavior Bible, which led us to enroll in Training With Instinct (TWI), YCA's online training program.

TWI has been an incredible foundation for us. The training resources, trainer guidance, and weekly calls gave us real structure and direction when we didn't know where else to turn. Connecting with other people going through similar challenges with their reactive dogs was invaluable too. We never felt like we were doing this alone.

Since flying to England for in-person training wasn't exactly in the cards, TWI was the next best thing. 😂 It gave us the tools and confidence to keep working with Kennedy every single day.

If you're feeling stuck or overwhelmed with a reactive dog, TWI is worth every bit of your time and money. Their understanding of reactivity is unmatched, and it's clear they genuinely care about both ends of the leash. 🐾❤️

Vinnie (my Staffy mix) and I recently completed YCA's 5-day bootcamp and it was one of the best decisions I've made. A week ago, if you'd told me I'd be confidently letting my dog off lead in public, I'd have smiled, nodded...and quietly thought you were completely mad.

Vinnie’s boisterous nature had become exhausting. Every person, every dog, every leaf blowing across the pavement apparently deserved investigating at full speed. Walks had turned into a daily workout, he had absolutely no 'off switch' when out and about, and I didn't know how to help us.

The team at YCA have been brilliant from start to finish. They're incredibly knowledgeable, approachable and genuinely invested in helping both you and your dog succeed. Everything is explained clearly and in a way that's easy to put into practice. Some of the techniques had a genuinley instant impact (which I'm still amazed by), while others have taken consistency and persistence, but that's all part of the process.

The difference in Vinnie after just those five days has been unbelievable. Walks are enjoyable again, I understand him so much better, and I feel so much more confident handling different situations. More than anything, it's given us both our freedom back.

One of the unexpected bonuses has also been meeting some lovely fellow dog owners. It's such a welcoming environment where everyone supports and encourages one another, making the whole experience even more enjoyable.

Thank you to everyone at YCA for all your help and support.

If you're reading reviews wondering whether the 5-day bootcamp is worth it….book it. You won't regret it.

Never thought we would see Luna out and about in the real world the academy has truly changed our lives and as well for Luna he is a much happier dog knowing how to express himself calmer to dogs and people with out  causing a mental breakdown from across the road 😂

Simon says…do this course!

I had made so many excuses for my dog, Simon, over the past two years. "Oh bless him, he’s a rescue" was my mantra! But I finally came to realise that life had become so restricted and stressful that we couldn't go on as we were. We had incrementally shut down so many aspects of our life just to manage Simon’s behaviour and keep everyone safe e.g. walking early to avoid other dog walkers, no more visitors to the house, shutting him away in the garage before the postman came, and gradually going out less and less. We genuinely felt we were doing the right thing at the time because...  "bless him, he's a rescue!" We were trying to keep everyone safe, but we were all leading a very limited life.

A good friend recommended Yorkshire Canine Academy and …WOW! What a week!

Is it hard work? Yes, but so is constantly restraining a reactive dog and apologising for it!
Is it expensive? Yes, but so is the price you pay for shutting yourself indoors with a reactive dog.
Is it emotional? Yes, but put on those big girl pants and just get through it.

The trainers at YCA are absolutely amazing—not all superheroes wear capes! They are so knowledgeable and supportive that you feel in safe hands from day one. Their systematic approach is completely science-backed. The processes are clear, and they provide plenty of opportunities to practise everything multiple times under close, patient supervision.

The other dog owners on the course are all in similar situations, so there is absolutely no judgement or embarrassment - only support. They celebrate wins with you and spur you on during the tricky bits. There was a real sense of shared celebration by the end of the week, with every single one of us being genuinely delighted in every dog's progress.

As a bonus, two of my sons came along to watch and learn the techniques, and they were so inspired by the whole YCA team that now they both want to be dog trainers!

I’m so excited to get started enjoying life alongside Simon. We have so many adventures on the horizon!! He deserves it because "bless him, he's a rescue dog!!"

If you’re living in restriction and despair, Simon says... just do this course.
It won't just train your dog; it will give you your life back.

Otis was reactive to joggers runners cats , some dogs and people , his walks were getting very stressful for us and after having 2 other trainers and calming medications I found YCA on instagram , started following them , it’s been the best thing we’ve done , the team are fantastic , Owain Toni Alex and Lee are caring understanding and so helpful, they’ve given us support and knowledge which has turned Otis into a calmer more focused dog , we now have more confidence and control on our walks - no more avoiding all his triggers , we honestly can’t recommend these guys enough , you even get lifetime help and social classes on a weekend , ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

The bootcamp has been a game changer for us. Our lab Bramble was terrorising people who walked through our farm, so much so, she was making our lives an absolute misery. Not only that, she started lunging and barking at people we'd invited to the house. The final straw for us was when one of my husbands grandkids stuck their hand through the fence into our yard, and she tried to grab it. Enough was enough, so off to bootcamp we went. This is not a cheap experience, but what price can one put on peace of mind? I was constantly having to go out to see who was about when she started barking her head off, and became fearful of her behaviour since the arrival of my first grandson a few months ago. I cannot praise the staff highly enough. They guide you through the week and offer you guidance to ensure you get the most out of the experience. At the beginning of the week, none of the dogs mixed, but by the end of the week, we were all walking together, both on and off lead. The grand finale was all 15 dogs and owners sitting together (in fairly close proximity) in one room. It was truly mindblowing. There is homework to do prior to your arrival at the camp, which is to ensure your dog has a good marker. The pre camp videos explain everything fully, and if you're really wanting a better life for yourself, and more importantly for your dog, you need to follow the advice given to ensure a greater chance of success upon arriving for your week at the academy.  We've now got a completely different dog to the one we arrived with. Bramble is a lot more chilled around people, and I've had people at my fence and not even known they were there until I opened my door because Bramble has been able to ignore them. The biggest 'wow' incident was last Saturday as we were parked up at a service station. I was giving Bramble a drink in the boot of the car, when unbeknownst to me, a young child had walked up to the car and was looking at Bramble. I was startled when I turned round, as Bramble had not reacted at all. Before bootcamp, she'd have lunged out at the child and started barking given half a chance. She actually wouldn't have done because I would have had hold of her, but therein lies the difference. I've gone from being super hypervigilant when out, to being relaxed because she is no longer reactive. The academy do use e collars, and I know some folk reading this will immediately be put off by that. However, if you don't want to live in a hypervigilant state, and you want your dog to lead a life of freedom, then I would urge you to gain a lived experience of how these collars used CORRECTLY will liberate a reactive dog. They are NOT cruel used correctly. If you're wondering if this training facility can help, I'm here to tell you that it absolutely can.

Quite simply, bootcamp works. Sir Bert  (crowned at bootcamp …forever Sir Bert and no longer high-alert Bert ♥️) only needs a look and a word from me, this morning, in the house … and  no one can quite believe how this alpha boss-attitude mini schnauzer fur boy, who reacted to every person and noise (as if his sole duty in life was to be the guard meerkat over his family), and drove us half mad at times, is operating on a palpably different mode already. It is a much better life for us all, dogs and humans, and it’s only been a few days.

It is important to say why this works. The carefully constructed programme is exceptional. The people facilitating the camp are beyond exceptional. I cannot commend enough the professionalism, dedication, care, empathy and overall brilliant-ness of every person who has helped shaped our progress this week.

Mark, move, pay is forever etched in my mind and I now have a constructive toolkit to move  progress forward. So happy and so grateful and looking forward  to continuing the work … 🙏 ☺️

I could spot prey from a mile away and would immediately be on edge, watching for the thing that might distract her and send her off. Another dog running over? Cue instant stress. Settling in public? Almost impossible.

Our walks became a game of avoidance. I’d cross the road, turn around or take another route to avoid dogs, while my cortisol levels went through the roof scanning for prey. There’s a reason I had a tracker on her! 😂

I also had to recognise that I was part of the problem. My anxiety meant I would avoid situations, which probably reinforced the very behaviours I was trying to prevent.

After a consultation call with Fred at Yorkshire Canine Academy, I was booked onto the 5 day bootcamp a couple of weeks later.

I’ll be honest… I was sceptical. Bailey wasn’t food motivated and I genuinely didn’t believe we could achieve loose lead walking, a reliable recall AND neutrality around other dogs.

One week later, I’m completely blown away by the difference.

We have a loose lead walk, something I genuinely thought was impossible for my spaniel who previously dragged me everywhere. Her recall is solid. We can drop the ball when asked (IYKYK 😂). She is calmer, more settled in cafe’s. Most importantly, I now have the skills and confidence to know what to do in different situations.

But the biggest change isn’t just Bailey. It’s our relationship.

Despite me being “stricter”, she loves me more. I understand her better, she understands what I’m asking of her, and I’m enjoying our walks again rather than constantly being on high alert…she is a pleasure over a chore!

The 5 days themselves were brilliant, but what really sets Yorkshire Canine Academy apart for me is the ongoing support. Being local, we can continue attending the weekly socialisation classes, and having access to the trainers and further training materials means this doesn’t just end when you leave bootcamp.

If you’re sitting there thinking “my dog could never do that”…I was that person.

I honestly cannot recommend the team at Yorkshire Canine Academy enough. 🐾❤️

Bailey and I have gone from me constantly managing her to actually enjoying being a team. And that, for me, is worth everything.

Biggest Tip to anyone booked on: embrace everything and make sure you do the pre-work beforehand religiously, it pays dividends during the week!

I can't recommend the Yorkshire Canine Academy enough. We attended bootcamp with Jax, our dog reactive German Shepherd a couple of weeks ago having watched many of Jacob's videos on YouTube. To say we were impressed by the whole set up would be an understatement! And the results were plain to see in all the dogs by the end of the week.

Richard Sue & Jax

TL:DR - Is the bootcamp expensive? Yes. Is it worth it? Without a doubt, yes, book it. I just walked my dog down the street on a lead without incident - enough said 🤣

On to the details: Our dog, Havoc, is an ~8 month old Welsh Collie and was the absolute spiciest of dogs - we rescued him 3-4 months ago and were mislead on his reactivity challenges. Havoc was reactive to dogs, bikes, people, kids, random sounds - you name it, he was probably reactive to it - and we were completely unequipped to handle it.

Havoc’s world had shrunk to nothing and along with that, our other dog was suffering and we weren’t able to enjoy any experience out of the house with him.

We tried 3 other trainers without any success and reached out to YCA in desperation as a last resort. We had our initial conversation with Elisha, who was able to answer all our questions and give us the peace of mind needed to book on.

There was pre-work to do prior to the bootcamp, including an online course. My only piece of constructive feedback I can give for the whole experience is that there were some elements of the online training that could have been better explained - our group had a WhatsApp with the trainers that was set up a few weeks before and I think there were quite a few places we’d either missed things or misinterpreted them and that could probably reduce a lot of the pre-course queries.

Onto the boot camp: Day 1 is intense. I’d been hiding Havoc from as much as possible since we got him because he was such a nightmare, and I wasn’t prepared for what I saw from him on that first day. Both he and I had a breakdown, the emotions of the last three months all came out in one go - but Toni and Owaine were so lovely and helped to reassure me that it’d start to turn around.

Day 2 is where it all changed for us. The punishment work we did started to drive that change in Havoc that meant, for the first time, we were actually able to, by the end of the day, walk into the arena without him barking and lunging at everyone and everything. I’d never used an e-collar or prong prior to the course and it was all done in a safe, ethical way that gives the dogs their freedom and actually gets results by giving the dogs clarity.

The trainers tailored everything to Havoc’s needs, helping to get the right training opportunities at the right time. And they were so patient with making sure we understood everything and really dedicated to the dogs and peoples safety.

By day 5 we were in a pub with all the other dogs, I couldn’t believe it. But the support doesn’t stop there - Havoc has trouble walking well on the lead and even as we were wrapping up bootcamp we started working on an e-collar heel supporting me to keep this up at home with ongoing support. Post bootcamp Havoc is mostly disinterested in people, bikes and kids now, we are still working on dogs but there has been a tremendous improvement.

I want to give a special shout out to Toni, Alex and Lee - who have gone above and beyond in helping Havoc to continue improving and to offer me support through the process. I would highly recommend doing the ongoing life skills sessions and socialisation on a Saturday. I found the socialisation a bit intimidating at first as there are so many dogs there and Havoc is still a bit hyped up in these settings (no where like before) but the trainers are great at getting relevant activities for people and getting you to do the things that are going to keep your dog learning. They also ensure that anyone who needs a bit of extra support has it, which I am so so grateful for as I am still a work in progress, but the ongoing support from YCA even after the bootcamp is astounding.

Havoc is by no means perfect, and it isn’t going to be a straight upwards line, I know we will have setbacks, but the main thing is that I’m confident to handle it and I know YCA are there to help. They really are the last training company you will ever need.

After being completely at our wits end with our French bull dog Timmy we were lucky enough to find YCA, after trying other trainers and it failing.
Timmy had bitten our post man, constantly barked at our neighbours fence, bitten 3-4 other people in our garden and was extremely reactive to other dogs. I was walking him at crazy times so I wouldn’t see anyone and walks were not enjoyable whatsoever, I actually dreaded taking him out. If I saw another dog even in the distance Timmy would go wild screeching, pulling, barking. My older dogs life became more limited with Timmy being so reactive, everything revolved around Timmy, no holidays with our dogs, walks on beaches, off lead walks.
Fast forward two weeks, we completed the 5 day boot camp last week and I actually cannot believe I have the same dog.
By day 3 we were on a group walk together, that afternoon all 10 reactive dogs were laid on beds in the same room and by Friday we were sat in a pub eating lunch with all 10 Dogs laid by our feet, I actually cried with happiness at the pub.
I met Owain for my consultation and he promised me I would be sat in the pub with Timmy by the 5th day and I said there’s no way! But he was right ☺️
We now have 2 well behaved dogs and it’s opened a whole new world up for Timmy and our family. His recall is 10x better than my other dogs! He hasn’t reacted to another dog since day 1 on boot camp and he just seems a generally happy, more playful but relaxed dog.
YCA gave me the 3/4 commands to use which Timmy full understands now, we have our own language and it works! Also the knowledge to keep on going with my training going forward. I am also extremely lucky to live 5 minutes from the academy where every Saturday we can attend socialisation classes and go for a big group walk meaning he’s meeting even more dogs and I can chat with the trainers for any more advice I may be needing..this is incredible and not something you’ll find with other trainers!
I can’t thank Sam, Owain, Alex, Simao, Toni, Melissa and all the other trainers who helped enough, they have literally changed mine and Timmy’s life.

I honestly can’t thank YCA enough for the experience Kapser my 18mth old male Weimaraner and I have had over the last five days.

When we started the bootcamp, my main goals were to improve Kapser’s confidence and work on his lead reactivity towards other dogs. Like many owners dealing with reactivity, walks could sometimes feel stressful and unpredictable, and I wanted to learn how to better support him and help him navigate the world with more confidence.

What made this bootcamp so valuable was that we completed it alongside 13 other dogs, all with similar challenges. Over those five days, I watched Kapser grow in confidence in ways I didn’t think possible. More importantly, I learned how much my own handling, body language and mindset could influence him. The course wasn’t about someone else training my dog, it was about teaching us how to work together as a team in real life situations.

Seeing Kapser able to remain calmer around other dogs, make better choices, and look to me for guidance instead of reacting has been incredibly rewarding. Every small win felt huge and by the end of the bootcamp I realised just how far we’d both come in such a short space of time, even shedding a few happy relieved tears on our drive home.

The YCA team were knowledgeable, supportive and genuinely invested in the success of every dog and owner there. No question was too much, no challenge was dismissed, and every achievement was celebrated. Their passion for what they do is obvious from the moment you meet them.

I’m leaving this bootcamp with a more confident dog, but also as a more confident owner. Most importantly, Kapser and I have a stronger bond and a better understanding of each other than ever before.

Thank you YCA, for giving us the tools, confidence and ongoing support to continue this journey long after the five days have ended. I’m incredibly proud of Kapser, and so grateful for everything we’ve learned together and that’s all down to you and your amazing team ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

A trainer we used in Belgium said Ozzy, our five year old black rescue Lab, will never change, he will always remain highly reactive towards other dogs.
Even our usual vet said the same, just a few days before we arrived at YCA for a five day boot camp.

On the first day at boot camp everyone could see just how bad Ozzy’s reactivity was when they brought out a stooge dog.
Ozzy went mental.

However, during the course of the week he improved every day, and after three lunchtimes in the pub, where he laid down and ignored all the other dogs, we knew we would have a dog that we would be proud of.

In October 2025, Ozzy pulled me over in the forest, breaking my hip in the process.
We have since returned to the forest and passed other dogs without incident.

But the return trip home to Belgium really showed it was all worthwhile.
At the Le Shuttle terminal building in Folkestone we took Ozzy inside with us so we could have a coffee and a bite to eat before boarding our train.
There were dozens of dogs inside with their owners, some laying quietly and some barking at Ozzy.
Ozzy never flinched, he ignored all of them, we were so proud of him.

We cannot praise the YCA team enough, every single one of them gave clear and precise instructions about using the proper equipment to control and correct Ozzy.
A special mention to Melissa, who gave plenty of one on one with us and Ozzy.

It was money well spent!

Sorry for the long post, but if you have a reactive dog, this is worth reading. For years, we thought we had tried everything with Charlie, our German Shepherd/Wolf Dog cross. Trainers, books, online courses and advice from well-meaning people all failed to change things. After he was attacked by two American Bully XLs in a public dog park, Charlie became reactive to dogs he didn’t know. Walks became stressful, carefully planned and limited to places where we could avoid triggers.

Then I saw a YouTube video from YCA about helping reactive dogs. They described our exact problem, even our type of dog, so I signed up for the free course and then the bootcamp. I’ll be honest: after so many previous disappointments, I felt both hopeful and sceptical. On day one, we were told that by day five our dogs would be walking off lead and we’d all be going to the pub together. At that point, with dogs barking and reacting all around us, it felt impossible.

But day by day, everything changed. The bootcamp wasn’t just about training the dogs; it was about teaching us as owners how to guide better decisions, reward the right behaviour and calmly move them away from the wrong ones. The change in Charlie was rapid, dramatic and genuinely life changing.

By day four, I felt a weight lift that I hadn’t realised I’d been carrying for years. On day five, Charlie was off lead in a public park for the first time in years, and yes, we all went to the pub for lunch with the other dogs. There were only a couple of tiny incidents, and thankfully none from Charlie.

The course wasn’t just for big dogs either. There were dogs of all shapes and sizes, including a French Bulldog, collies, a greyhound cross, German Shepherds and a Staffie. If your life has become about managing your dog’s behaviour, avoiding places and planning everything around triggers, I honestly believe this course is worth considering. You do need to put the work in beforehand and follow the instructions, but the rewards can be more than you imagine.

Charlie had been restricted to being on a lead for years due to his reactivity, we are now confident enough to let him off lead in public places, it has been less than a week since we did the training course when we took the video attached to this review, this is how quickly all our lives have been transformed.

One of the best parts was that YCA only asked for a deposit upfront and said we could pay the balance on the final day if we were happy with the results. We were among the first to pay. Since the bootcamp, we’ve been able to go to places that had been out of bounds for years. In less than a month, we went from feeling restricted to having our lives back — and, most importantly, we got Charlie back.

We had a very reactive bull lurcher, after bootcamp we have a well behaved lurcher. The training was not just the dog but for us even more. All done in a respectful way. We even got to stop on site in our camper.
Fully recommend this place if you are having issues with your dogs behaviour just ring or email them .

I was sceptical about training courses having seen so many on Facebook but I am so glad I decided to sign up. It is true that by the end of the week we were sat in a pub having a meal with all the dogs sitting quietly at our feet. It had made such a difference to both myself and our dog. Walks are now such a pleasure. Worth every penny.

I’ve just done boot camp. Five days and Poppy has changed. She’s calmer. She doesn’t bark at passers by from the house or the garden. Her recall is brilliant. I’m not saying she’s perfect - she’s not, as a little incident today proved, but I have all the tools to manage those incidents and the confidence to use them. We have to keep
Going and I will probably need to check back in with the guys over some issues I’m not quite sure about how to handle, but I know they will know.. thank you so much all of you.

Life-Changing Transformation for My Reactive Malinois!

If you are even remotely thinking about booking a bootcamp with the YCA, stop hesitating—it is an absolute no-brainer. Yes, it is an investment, but it is an investment in your dog’s future and your own peace of mind. It has completely changed our lives.

In April 2026, I attended the 5-day bootcamp with my two-and-a-half-year-old Belgian Malinois, Shadow. Before finding the YCA, our world had become incredibly small. Shadow had been attacked by two different dogs on two separate occasions when he was younger, which left him severely reactive. On walks, he would lunge and bark at other dogs to the point where I couldn't take him to any public places. We were restricted to walking him only on quiet country roads, constantly on edge.

The transformation after just five days at the YCA is nothing short of a miracle 🙏

To give you an idea of how effective this training is: on the Friday afternoon—the final day of the bootcamp—we were all sat inside the pub together with 17 previously reactive dogs. It’s not a lie when the YCA tells you they’ll have you all in the pub on Friday, and I've attached a photo here to prove it! Seeing 17 dogs who used to struggle just being near another dog, all relaxing together in a busy environment, was unbelievable.

Since completing the bootcamp, we have been able to take Shadow everywhere with us. He is experiencing a completely different lifestyle now. Unbelievably, we are even able to have him off-lead a lot of the time! Shadow is significantly more relaxed, confident, and seems so much more fulfilled.

A massive, heartfelt thank you to the phenomenal team at the YCA—in particular Toni, Elisha, Simao, Owain, Cait, Alex, Melissa, and Pablo. Your expertise, patience, and understanding of complex dog behaviour gave both Shadow and me the tools we desperately needed.

If you are struggling with a reactive dog and feel like you've run out of options, trust the YCA. It is worth every single penny and more. Thank you all for giving us our lives back!❤️

When I first arrived, I was very skeptical of everything, from the equipment used, to the length of the course, I was even unsure it would work at all with my dog (reactive). But after just 2 days, 16 reactive dogs were walking on a field, just a couple metres apart with no issues. It was genuinely magic. The staff explain why the tools they use are beneficial and how they aren’t as evil as they seem. By Thursday, most dogs (if not all) had amazing recall off lead, didn’t react to any dogs in public and by Friday, were all in a pub just laying down being good pups. The staff there were all incredible as well, none of them were mean or pushy, they were patient with us and the dogs, they gave so much good advice and would answer literally any question with confidence. I never would’ve imagined the course to go so well

Yorkshire Canine Academy has been a game changer for our Frenchie, Bruce. Before starting reactive boot camp, he was incredibly reactive with both dogs and people. We couldn’t trust him off lead, and every walk felt tense. We were nervous, he was nervous and it showed.

Three weeks after finishing boot camp, we finally feel ready to put this into words. Not because we had nothing good to say, but because we wanted to reflect on the whole journey: before, during and after.

Boot camp gave Bruce structure, daily interaction and a safe environment to learn. He’s not perfect yet and we’re not pretending he is. He still has moments, and we know this is going to take time and more support from the at YCA. But the progress he’s made already is huge, and the confidence the team has given us is just as important as the work they’ve done with him.

When boot camp ended, we were honestly gutted. It had become such a positive routine for him. But we’ve kept the momentum going by attending the Saturday morning re‑socialisation classes every single week. “Brucie Saturdays” have become part of our life now, and the continued support from the team means everything.

Our confidence in Bruce is really starting to grow and it’s so lovely to see those little moments where he gets to just be a “dog”, instead of living life through our own insecurities.

What makes YCA different is that they don’t offer quick fixes. They give you real tools, real understanding and real support. They change how you handle your dog, how you think, and how you react and that’s what creates long‑term change.

A huge shoutout to Owain, Kirky, Alex, Toni and Mel for their patience, guidance and genuine care for both us and Bruce. We appreciate everything you’ve done so far, and we’ll definitely be continuing our journey with the YCA family.

P.s…Bruce said he will get you next time, Owain 😄

Our retriever was very difficult to walk on the lead and too excited to see people and dogs that we stopped going into pubs and cafes. The team at YCA helped us understand how to teach our dog to regulate his energy and this has transformed how he interacts with the world around him. Ok to be lively on off lead walks. Able to sit quietly in a cafe.

My daughter is currently doing training here and she just LOVES it. Along with this she's training her own dog and the change in her within 2 days is just phenomenal! These guys really are magical! I can't recommend using YCA enough. They have 100% success rate, are lovely people and are in a beautiful setting, they very much deserve 5 stars, I'd give more I'd I could!

I waited a week after Boot Camp before writing this review because I wanted to make sure we could carry on the work they started.
Having a reactive dog for the past five years has been tough. We'd tried so many different approaches and worked with several trainers, and by the time we found Yorkshire Canine Academy, it felt like our last chance. We'd resigned ourselves to solitary walks and had pretty much given up on having friends round to the house. Thank goodness we decided to take that final step.
There's still work to do, but life looks very different after Boot Camp. We now enjoy regular walks at least twice a day, at normal times, without constantly worrying about who or what we might come across.
So what did they actually do at Boot Camp? They gave us the tools to communicate properly with our dog and, just as importantly, the confidence to trust ourselves. They showed us that while training tools have their place, connection, communication and confidence are what really make the difference.
The support before Boot Camp was good. There was homework to do, and they were very clear about what was expected. The week itself was an incredible experience. We had guidance from so many people, all giving consistent advice and support. At no point did we feel judged or patronised; instead, we received kind, patient and consistent coaching throughout.
We arrived with a very reactive dog and honestly had no idea what to expect. I was terrified about how she might react to the people and other dogs around her. My brain stopped working for at least the first 24 hours. But there was always someone available to answer questions and to let us know what to do now, what to do next.
Once we got through the anxiety of that first day, everything started to fall into place. Throughout the week, they focused on what we were doing well, while helping us correct what needed improving. There was always someone keeping an eye on us when we were working with our dog, which gave us a huge amount of reassurance.
We were already using a prong collar before Boot Camp, but we weren't using it correctly, and the difference since learning how to use it properly has been remarkable. I was also very sceptical about the e-collar. Like many people, I'd read plenty of negative opinions about them. However, our dog has responded incredibly well to it, and although she wears it, we rarely need to use it.
I wish I could mention every member of the team individually because they all played a part in our journey. Simāo was a fantastic “pack leader”, Kirky was always there, knowledgeable and approachable, Kate and Melissa kind and gently guided us throughout, Kelly calm, straightforward and reassuring, Toni always helpful, and Alex was just as happy to lend us a lead as to give us some confidence and courage when we needed it.
Thank you all. You may well have changed our lives.
Mercedes

What a fantastic experience. Bootcamp was well structured, staff all knowledgeable and friendly. I learned how I messed up my dog by giving conflicting information (not realising I was doing it). Yesterday I was walking my dog out at a normal time on a busy street.  A dog approximately 4 metres away from us kicked off exactly like my dog has done for 2 1/2 years. My dog not only didnt react, he wasn't loading either. Unbelievable.  The owners of the other dog apologised profusely. My reply, "Please don't apologise. My dog was exactly like yours." I know I have to keep up the work/standards with my dog but I am hopeful. Can't wait to go back to YCA on a Saturday to get feedback from experts.

It's a week now since we completed the 1st June Bootcamp. Reggie, our 15 month old Airedale Terrier was a struggle. We consciously avoided places where there would be other dogs as he was just so desperate to meet them and so he would pull, zigzag and sit down or turn around. We couldn't go into a cafe or anywhere socially. We were spending a great deal of money taking Reggie to dog fields to exercise him. We attended an assessment at YCA with Alex and with his advice and recommendations enrolled for a Bootcamp commencing 1st June. We soon realized that we were not alone in having a difficult dog (that was the start of not feeling trapped). The initial briefings and discussions gave us a timetable and plan that sounded sensible. The tools and techniques that we would learn initially made us uneasy but the trainers (Simao and Kirky) reassured us that they were essential to a positive outcome (and boy, were they right). Every day and every exercise stretched us and our dog, but being in a positive group of owners and trainers, all striving to improve and build our and our dogs behaviour, relationships and understanding, began to become clear as the days unfolded. By the Wednesday we were doing things with our dog that on the Monday we would have thought impossible. For us, the prong collar proved to be such a useful tool, the trainers soon taught us how to be effective in its use when combined with effective use of the leash. The ecollar was something we weren't too sure about at first, but again, the trainers were excellent in giving us the understanding of when and how to use it effectively, and Reggie responded so well that in practice we barely needed to resort to it as the associated commands we learnt/adopted in conjunction with it were almost always all that was required to obtain the control we desired. The group exercises in the arena and out in the fields (going from on leash to off leash) were so encouraging; the pace of progress was impressive under the watchful eyes of the trainers (Simao. Alex, Elisha and Melissa) who were so diligent in offering really great advice and answers to any questions. The group off-site visits were so good; Adel recreation ground, Golden Acre Park, Temple Newsam and Roundhay Park (and the Friday pub visit) were all things we could never have envisaged us doing on the Monday. We are now building on what we have learnt. Obviously Reggie has the occasional lapse but we now have a happier and more relaxed dog and have a growing confidence in how to manage him. We can now enjoy comfortable walks with him, without having to avoid people/dogs/places, and can stop off for a pleasant cafe break (even when the Yorkshire rain is tormenting us). For anyone who is considering attending a YCA course, I would wholeheartedly say "Do it"; the people at YCA are great, the course content is so well structured and they provide support and advice for every foible your dog may have; plus the opportunity to interact with other owners and their dogs over the week really boosts confidence and belief that a great outcome is achievable. Thank you YCA, you are all a great team with a great product offering.

We had a reactive Doberman who lunged and pulled towards every dog in the street. We struggled to have a peaceful walk in the parks, cities or on hikes.
There are so many materials and tutorials online, and we tried plenty of them but nothing really helped. We taught our dog tricks, played with him to drain his energy and we could see how smart he is. However, we were unable to stop bad behaviour, build reliable recall and have confidence in letting him off leash.
All these had become our new reality by the end of the 5 days bootcamp. With the help of great dog trainers of YCA we now can enjoy time with our dog and understand how to communicate with him clearly.
A huge part of the bootcamp is that you learn alongside with your dog. You will learn how to make your dog understand exactly what you mean, what’s bad and what’s good, how to approach other dogs and humans, how to relax and play. You will have everything at your disposal to continue this journey without the need of further supervision.
The bootcamp also equips you with tools like e-collar that will truly liberate your dog. You will learn how these tools work and see that they are not scary, don’t make harm to your dog, but work as a safety belt.
We would also like to acknowledge the help of Simão and Alex. They answered many of our questions and resolved all the frustration we might have had initially. These gentlemen payed close attention to our specific needs and the nature of our dog. A huge thanks to them and all the staff at YCA.

From technical side, the parking is big and convenient, there is a coffee machine and a fridge with cold drinks any of the clients may use free of charge. We went to see different environments at the academy and outside, including a coffee shop and a restaurant as well as parks. YCA has any equipment ready and always in abundance.

We are absolutely happy to recommend YCA and prove that the before/after videos are 100% accurate. We were very skeptical that our dog will substantially transform in such a short time. However, the bootcamp worked wonders for each of 17 dogs that week.

It's day 3 at home after a week at Bootcamp with the Yorkshire Canine Academy.  Lena, our lurcher cross, has been transformed into a calmer dog. She no longer pulls on the lead or whines when we stand and chat to people. She calmly walks by our side or in front in the park or streets and likes to say hello to any dogs passing.

We were apprehensive about the use of the tools (e-collar/prong collar) but the trainers put our minds at ease by showing us how to put them on our dog so as not to stress her out.

Lena was fairly unhappy and sensitive about getting out of the car each day for training but once the training got underway she actually enjoyed being with the other dogs in our group.

I would highly recommend the YCA to any dog owners who are struggling with their dog's behaviour.

Thank you to all the trainers who have helped us change Lena for the better.

Thank you!

As I sit here just 48 hours after completing the bootcamp with my Cocker Spaniel, Ernie, I can genuinely say our lives have already changed immensely for the better.

This weekend, we’ve spent hours exploring the forest, walking along the canal, and playing hide-and-retrieve in the park just five minutes from my house—all completely off lead. We’ve passed dogs left, right, and centre without a single reaction. He even happily lay down in the pub for over an hour while I enjoyed a pint. To top it all off, his heel work has been immaculate all weekend.

Just a week ago, none of this would have been possible without stress and constant worry. Would he come back when called? Would he react to a dog 20 metres away? Would he spend the whole time whining and crying in the pub? I found myself avoiding situations like these. Now, I can’t wait for my alarm to go off in the morning so we can head to the park, and I look forward to finishing work so we can get back out into the forest to explore together.

While we still have plenty of work ahead of us, I now feel confident that I can be a much better owner for Ernie. He is clearly more fulfilled and content, and in return he’s become the sweetest boy at home. When we’re not out training, playing, or walking, he’s simply curled up nearby, completely relaxed.

I’d like to say a huge thank you to everyone involved in the bootcamp, but especially:

Melissa – for giving me the confidence and reassurance during the free 1-to-1 call that the course was the right thing for us. She also provided great guidance on Ernie’s recall and what to expect when I got home, particularly when I was struggling to create enough distance to practise effectively.

Simao – for his calm, knowledgeable guidance throughout the week and for taking extra time to ensure Ernie’s e-collar was set up perfectly. It was clear he wasn’t prepared to take any chances when it came to getting things right.

Elisha – for tailoring Ernie’s play session to his needs, recognising that he was a little closed down, and very politely telling me to stop being a wuss and not be afraid to play with him a bit more enthusiastically!

These are the moments that have really stuck with me, but Kirky, Alex, Kate and Kelly were all fantastic too. I was also incredibly lucky to be part of such a friendly group of fellow boot campers and their beautiful dogs.

The biggest change isn’t just in Ernie’s behaviour—it’s in the opportunities now available to him. Rather than being restricted by his worries and anxieties, he can spend more time doing what a spaniel was born to do: exploring new places, using his nose, playing, learning and embracing the world around him. The bootcamp has given me the tools, knowledge and confidence to guide him through that journey, and seeing him happier, more fulfilled and more confident is worth every minute of effort. Thank you for helping me give Ernie the life he deserves, and for helping us build a partnership that will allow us to enjoy many more adventures together.

I dont even know where to start!!!!

She was reactive to people and dogs and just overall scared of everything, by the end of the week she was off lead with other dogs and even having a cuddle with one of the trainers, Alex!
