They accommodated to the weather as it was the middle of a heatwave and had us start at 8am instead of 10am so that the dogs weren’t out in the scorching sun, granted we got stuck in a thunderstorm with hail stones and torrential rain which wasn’t fun for us but was definitely better for the dogs🫠

I had my doubts about the bootcamp working at the beginning of the week but by day 3 you really see it all fall into place and the difference it really does make to not only the dogs but to the owners too. The stress and panic you feel before you leave to go on a walk because you know your dog is going to kick off at anything and everything turns into excitement and pride knowing you can go sit in the pub or go into the shops and not have any problems or if anything were to happen you have the tools to be able to communicate efficiently with your dog and tell them if they’ve done something right or wrong.

If you are considering the bootcamp, definitely do it, it is the best decision I have made and I am so happy I can now give my dog the life of freedom and fulfilment that she deserves!

Thank you to everyone at the Yorkshire Canine Academy and the difference you have made for us.

I recently completed the Reactivity Boot Camp with my Border Terrier, Shenzi. Shenzi has had dog reactivity for about 3 years. You have 360 vision, constantly looking for other dogs, working out the quickest escape route, panicking when you can't find one and then dealing with the inevitable fall out. I had previously had a face to face session with Kirky and found it really beneficial hence taking the plunge to do the Boot Camp.

WOW!!! The results are real. I never thought I'd be sitting in a pub with a whole load of dogs and walking through a really busy park with no reactions after five days of training. We’re now 2 months post bootcamp, & the results are incredible. We discovered YCA through social media and amazing reviews. The results have been mind-blowing—they trained Ste, who then taught me. Rex seems relieved, as if he finally understands us. Steve & Carla

After being to many trainers, these at the YCA are the most professional and knowledgeable. Being on  hand to deal with your problems. They are also extremely nice people. They made a tremendous difference to my dog , and left me with a lot of information on how to deal with my problem. The 5 day course is well worth the money. Ann and Sky

I have just completed a 5 day bootcamp at YCA with my 1 year old Cavapoo, Mabel.
Mabel has been reactive since she was a young puppy but her reactivity had increased in intensity over the past 5/6 months. She was reactive to people and dogs especially but also fearful of almost everything outside of our family circle.

Prior to getting Mabel, I had other dogs who I used to enjoy walks, hikes and holidays with. But all of that ended because of Mabel’s reactivity. Walks became a chore that I would only do very early morning and in the late evening to avoid contact with people and dogs as much as possible. During walks, I was constantly on edge and in a state of panic ‘just incase’ a dog or person appeared. The stress I felt daily was overwhelming and I honestly dreaded taking the dogs out for a walk.

I knew we couldn’t continue like it, non of us were enjoying life as we should be and I felt helpless that I was unable to communicate with Mabel in those moments of reactivity to make her feel safe.

I had been following YCA on instagram for a while and watching Jacob’s inspirational videos regarding his own battles with dog training so I decided to reach out to them for help.

I spoke to Elisha initially and she was really helpful and after sharing my issues, she assured me that they would definitely be able to help us. So I booked on the course immediately.

What a week we had, we battled through a heatwave and a walk in a thunderstorm with torrential rain and hail (a memory that will live with me forever ☺️) but the staff managed it all incredibly and the welfare of our dogs was always their main priority

In all honesty, I found the first couple of days of the course quite tough as I felt I was not able to communicate effectively with Mabel and i was not sure I was going to make it to the end. But a special thanks to Owain for supporting me when I felt like I’d hit a wall.

The knowledge and expertise of all staff and the way they advocate for our dogs was inspiring and they were always on hand to provide advice and support.

I have never been anywhere in public with Mabel because of her reactivity so the prospect of going to a pub for lunch absolutely terrified me, but she was the perfect dog the whole time and I was honestly blown away.

Our training journey has only just started but the dog I have come home with is not the same as the dog I started the course with and it’s something I hadn’t thought possible.

I would advise anyone who is considering taking the step to make contact with YCA asap, you will not regret it. The whole team are incredible ☺️

Owain, Simao, Alex, Mel, Elisha and Toni, I want to say thank you. You really made what I thought was impossible, possible and I cannot thank you all enough ☺️

YCA bootcamp is for anyone with a reactive dog who is responsible enough to want to change this behaviour. There is no judgement, no discrimination only support, guidance and a standard of professionalism and knowledge that changes everything.

Having completed bootcamp with my boxer dog Basil just over four weeks ago and attending two of the socialisation classes on a Saturday morning what can I say.

Pre bootcamp

Walks would be stressful for both of use.
Basil would wear a warning jacket ‘My dog needs space / reactive dog in training’.  He would wear a muzzle, a slip lead and a lead attached to me.  He would be walked early morning / late night or at times when I new it would not be busy.  He would not be left off lead as I did not trust myself of him.  He was not living his best life.

I had tried other trainers / methods, and nothing had worked.
After conducting my research, I arranged an online consultation with Simao.  We discussed the issues with my dog, and both agreed that the bootcamp would be a great fit.  I booked the bootcamp course the following day and could not wait to attend.
Prior to attending you are provided access to videos of pre bootcamp homework to do which are extremely useful.
Bootcamp w/c 30 March 2026

Was I nervous about attending – yes, but to see that there are other people in the same situation made me feel a little bit better.
There was no long introduction like you get in work meetings.  It was explained how the week would work and then we started.  The first couple of days are spent with the owners watching each other’s dogs and learning what their issues are, which made me feel more at ease that I was not the only one with a reactive dog.
After a couple of days, you get to the stage where all the dogs on the bootcamp are in the same arena laid on beds near each other (which is something that I never thought would happen with Basil).

On Thursday and Friday as a group you leave site and go out into the real world on walks through local parks and to a local pub for lunch (which is organised well).

On completion you receive a picture, certificate, and recommended homework.

All the staff make you feel welcome and that you are not alone in dealing with your dog’s issues.  From the first phone call with Simao to all the trainers during the course – Alex, Kirky, Owain, Elisha, Melissa, Toni for the payment side and everyone else who I have not named.

Post bootcamp

Was I slightly apprehensive about letting my dog off lead on my own, absolutely but I have worked on that.  Whenever possible he is off lead or on a flexi / long lead.

I have attended two socialisation classes since where he has been around other dogs that were not on his course, and this is building both our confidence.

Everything is still a work in progress, but I would like to thank the YCA for showing me how to use the tools to allow Basil freedom to be a dog and live his best life.  I wish I had done it sooner.

We have just finished our week at Yorkshire Canine Academy and wow—what a transformation.

We joined the boot camp this week with Zosha and Toby for several reasons: reactivity to dogs, people, and pulling on the lead. But the most heartbreaking issue was that they had become reactive toward each other. For the last three months, they had been tethered at opposite ends of the house to prevent further fights.

We genuinely thought we might have to rehome one of our beloved dogs for everyone’s safety.

After watching many of their videos, we contacted Yorkshire Canine Academy and arranged a consultation. From the start, Elisha was welcoming, reassuring, and incredibly thorough in explaining the process. She gave us practical steps to keep both us and the dogs safe at home before boot camp began.

I won’t lie—we still had serious reservations.

By Monday, we were very nervous (as was the rest of the group). But from the moment we arrived, everything was structured and supportive. We were introduced to the other dogs one by one and shown how to correctly use the training tools.

Throughout the week, we learned how to correct unwanted behaviours, how to set boundaries, and—most importantly—how to enjoy our time with our dogs again and help them coexist peacefully.

Simão was always there, hands-on, answering every question (even the slightly crazy ones!). Melissa guided our off-site walks, helping us spot triggers and correct things we might have missed, which really built our confidence.

A huge moment for us was when Alex managed to hand-feed Toby—something we never thought possible. Toby had never accepted food on lead or allowed a stranger to approach without reacting.

Owain led many of the sessions in the first few days. His consistency was key, and his unique way of handling repeating himself 5 times in a row (complete with toddler-style foot stomps!) kept us all smiling.

Watching all the dogs being resocialised was incredible—not just our own, but others who were even more reactive. The progress wasn’t just in the dogs, but in us as owners too.

At the start of the week, the idea of sitting in a pub together with all the dogs felt impossible. By Friday morning, we knew we could do it. And when we finally sat down together for lunch, it felt surreal—and emotional.

This experience didn’t just train our dogs. It gave us the confidence, skills, and belief that we *can* continue this at home.

Thank you to the entire team for giving us back our enjoyment, our confidence, and our family. We know there’s still work to do, but the support you’ve given us—and continue to give—means everything.

We truly couldn’t have done it without you.

Becca, Danny, Toby & Zosha 🐾

It was hard. My dog was miserable, and I was extremely sensitive about giving her the discipline she needed. At times, I genuinely thought I had broken her spirit — she looked unhappy and she couldn’t wait to get back to the car after the camp exercises. I know not every dog owner is this sensitive though 😅 so may not apply to you.

The camp started with core training: testing positive marker charging, learning negative marker charging, and conditioning the e-collar. The first few days the owners spent more time together learning the ins and outs and observing each others dogs, which I really enjoyed. Later on in the week we have spent more time with our dogs challenging their behaviour more and more.

The YCA team tested our dogs’ reactions after the exercises — and for anyone wondering whether it works, yes! There it was: my dog was calm. Focused on me. Looking for approval to sniff, engage, or change direction.

She became a perfect dog. She watched other dogs play off-leash and stayed with me. She was relaxed in the pub and strolled through parks without jittering when seeing other dogs. I got a dog!! Not just any dog. My dog. The dog I had waited for, researched for, read books about, watched documentaries about, and probably manifested under a full moon.
We did puppy training. We survived teething. We conquered “land shark” phase. We endured the zoomies. And you know what? He turned out… perfect. Calm. Mellow. Laid-back. So well behaved that people would say, “He’s such a good boy!” and I would casually reply, “Oh this? Yes. I made this.”
Naturally, in our wisdom, we thought:
“Well this has gone brilliantly. Let’s get another one.”
Enter Molly.
Molly is a year younger than her brother. Same mum. Same dad. Same breed. Same adorable labradoodle fluff. But as anyone with children—or houseplants—will tell you… same ingredients does not mean same outcome.
Where her brother is zen master, Molly is… espresso martini.
She is highly strung. Very nervous. Extremely reactive. To other dogs. To people. To birds. To cats. To squirrels. To dustbins. To leaves. To suspicious-looking blades of grass. To the concept of wind. Honestly, if air had feelings, she’d bark at it.
Oh my dear days!!
We sought help from a local behaviourist. At one point it was even suggested we try puppy Prozac—which we did, for well over a year. Sadly, it didn’t turn her into the chilled yoga instructor we’d hoped for.
But then—salvation came in the most modern of ways.
As a newly retired person armed with a smartphone and far too much scrolling time, I discovered a whole new world: TikTok. Instagram. Reels. Things I didn’t know existed and still don’t fully understand. During one particularly committed scrolling session, I stumbled across Yorkshire Canine Academy and Jacob Morgan and his team.
The videos were funny—but not fluffy nonsense. There was humour, yes. But there was also solid, serious knowledge behind it. So I decided to follow him. Not in a creepy hiding-in-the-bushes way, you understand. Just a healthy, algorithm-approved follow.
The more I watched, the more I thought: “He’s talking about Molly. Has he met Molly? Is Molly famous?”
So we reached out.
We had a Zoom call with AJ, who was informative, calm, and reassuring (all traits Molly does not possess). He suggested we try the Training with Instincts programme. I was… sceptical. Long-distance dog training? Through the internet? Was Molly going to need Wi-Fi?
But to cut a long story short—the team were phenomenal.
We sent in videos. Not polished, flattering videos. Oh no. The ugly ones. The “please ignore my shouting” ones. The “why is she barking at a hedge?” ones. And every single time, they were there—via Zoom (which they seem to run daily!) or through the WhatsApp group—with practical advice and encouragement.
“The uglier the video, the better,” they said. Which is lucky, because Molly does not do subtle.
We went right back to basics. Changed her food. Charged a marker (which is essentially dog language for “Yes! That! Do that again!”). We started simple focus exercises in the garden. Nothing dramatic. Nothing flashy.
And that simple focus work? Absolute game changer.
What began in the garden transferred to walks. Walks that were once a high-adrenaline obstacle course of potential triggers slowly became… manageable. Enjoyable, even. I stopped scanning the horizon like a meerkat on high alert.
Now, we know training is forever. Dogs aren’t flat-pack furniture you assemble once and admire. But most of what we’re doing now is reinforcing all the good things both dogs have learned.
YCA are always there to guide and support. They do use an e-collar protocol, which we personally chose not to follow—but that’s an individual choice. The support and knowledge are there regardless.
And we’ll continue to follow them—if only for the occasional giggle when Molly’s not reacting to a particularly offensive daisy.
Life with two labradoodles: one monk, one caffeine-fuelled life coach.
Would I change it?
Absolutely not.

We now enjoy country parks, river paddles, beach trips, caravan holidays, and dog-friendly restaurants, all without stress or anxiety.

We’ve also taken her to a flyball event and a dog show, as a spectator, completed the Walk 60 Miles With Your Dog challenge for Cancer Research (raising nearly £700), and tackled a wide range of environments including city walks, school runs, and busy public spaces. To finish the year, Rubix even attended Santa Paws with a pack of seven dogs — something we could never have imagined before visiting the YCA.

Rubix isn’t perfect — no dog is — but when challenges arise, we know how to handle them. The training works, and it lasts.

Before  visiting the YCA, we walked at unsociable hours and avoided dogs entirely.

I hesitated over the cost after spending more than £4,500 on unsuccessful trainers, but choosing the YCA was the best decision we ever made. If you’re unsure, don’t be — commit fully, practise consistently, and the results will follow.

The ongoing support from Jacob, Kirky, Elisha, and the entire YCA team has been outstanding. Their genuine interest in Rubix’s progress speaks volumes.

We are incredibly proud of how far Rubix has come — and endlessly grateful to the YCA for making it possible.

Background: I recently attended a five day Boot Camp at YCA and it’s made a huge, positive difference to me and my dog.

We re-homed Hector, a large guardian breed male, earlier this year. He had severe reactivity issues with certain dogs; not a specific breed or size or sex or whatever, it seemed to me he chose violence randomly whenever he fancied it, so I never knew what was coming.

Walks with Hector were stressful, I was always scanning for approaching dogs, wondering if he’d be in the mood to attempt to muller them or not. I’d avoid other dogs and places where I thought there might be other dogs. There were many incidents of violence and attempted violence.

Before attending the Boot Camp I’d done the usual – I’d read the books, watched “dog training” videos on YouTube etc. None of the things I read, watched or heard made any difference whatsoever to either me or Hector.

However, after the course, everything has changed.

After the course:

We can, and do, go anywhere we want to. In fact now I actively seek out other dogs, particularly reactive ones, and use them as training opportunities.

His “Heel” is fantastic.

His recall is rock solid.

He gets to run around off lead.

His play times are much more fun, he’s got a fantastic “out”.

His basic obedience, “Sit”, “Down”, “Stay” is hugely improved.

His reactivity has already decreased hugely, it’s a night and day difference to how he was before. I know what to look for before he decides to “kick off” and explain to him it’s neither necessary nor acceptable.

As for the course itself, I found some parts of it challenging and we were both knackered at the end of every day but it was so worth it.

The staff were all professional, friendly, approachable, knowledgeable and engaging and I can’t praise them highly enough.

Thanks to Elisha, Kirky, Owain, Alex and Toni for training me to be able to train my dog.

Thanks to Freds and Chloe for the stuff in the background.

Thanks to Owain and Alex for their help and support in dealing with the “Hickorys Incident” – cheers guys, I owe you a pint (or two).

Right, me and Hector are off to find some reactive dogs!

When we adopted Goose, our little rescue, we weren’t prepared for the level of reactivity he had. We were constantly avoiding certain streets, trails, or parks, and Goose was always on leash. We felt discouraged and quietly wondered if we’d taken on more than we could handle.

His reactivity wasn’t aggressive - it was social reactivity. He was overly friendly and didn’t know how to regulate his excitement around other dogs. But that didn’t make it any easier to manage, and it still kept him - and us - from enjoying the life we wanted together.

Then we found the Yorkshire Canine Academy.

It started with their YouTube videos - for the first time, we understood that Goose’s reactivity wasn’t just an obedience issue. It was about how he felt around his triggers.. and until we addressed that, nothing would truly change.

Since joining the TWI Program, everything has. With the support of Ian Kirk, Elisha King, and the entire YCA team, Goose has transformed - and so have we. We now enjoy fully off-leash hikes, confidently pass other dogs on trails, and live a life of freedom together. Goose has perfect recall, a solid heel, and clear understanding of helpful commands that keep us both safe and connected. We trust him - and he trusts us.

And best of all - YCA helped us achieve all of this without changing who Goose is. His friendliness and love for other dogs are still part of him, but now he has the structure, confidence, and understanding to navigate the world calmly and respectfully.

What makes YCA so special is that they didn’t just help us “control” Goose - they helped us learn who he was at heart. They showed us how to understand his needs, his temperament, and what fills his cup. This wasn’t about creating a dog who’s obedient because he’s scared to disobey - this was about building a confident, fulfilled dog who wants to listen, because he feels safe, understood, and free.

Goose is now the happiest, most balanced version of himself: curious, calm, goofy, and fully present with us. The bond we share today is because YCA taught us not just how to lead, but how to connect.

And the course isn’t just for your dog - it’s personal training for you. It teaches you how to be the kind of leader and trainer your dog truly needs. The skills, mindset, and theory you learn don’t just improve your dog’s life - they help you grow into the best version of yourself for your dog.

The program itself is brilliantly structured with step-by-step video lessons for every single training point. Jacob Morgan’s instruction in the videos is in a league of its own - he doesn’t just show what to do, he breaks down the why behind it, the timing, the mindset, and how it all fits together. His clear, detailed explanations paired with real-life examples make everything click - whether you’re brand new to training or feel like you’ve tried everything.

And through every group call and 1-on-1 session, Ian and Elisha were patient, thoughtful, and fully invested in our success. They never rushed an answer. They gave us their time, their guidance, and their belief - even when we weren’t sure of ourselves.

YCA didn’t just help us train our dog - they gave us back our joy, our freedom, and a bond with Goose we didn’t know was possible. If you’re struggling with reactivity or just want more from life with your dog, YCA will change everything.

Big thanks to the YCA.

I joined the Focus in Four Challenge after struggling with my young German Shepherd, Koko, who had developed reactivity towards both people and dogs during in-person training classes elsewhere. At just 6 months old, her reactivity was never addressed properly and I knew we needed a different approach. I wasn’t initially convinced that online training would work, but I’m so glad I gave YCA a chance, it’s been a game changer!

From the moment I enrolled, I had full access to a structured and easy to follow course with clear, engaging videos. I appreciated how the training encouraged moving at Koko’s pace, not just powering through content. We took our time working through each stage properly.

Whilst her reactivity wasn’t “fixed” in 4 weeks (which would be a big ask of any programme), there was a noticeable improvement in her behaviour. For instance, she was once completely overwhelmed when spotting other people or dogs (barking, lunging, unable to disengage) but one day, during outdoor training, another dog passed nearby and instead of reacting she re-directed her attention to me. That moment felt huge! A real testament to how effective the training is when applied consistently and patiently.

One of my favourite aspects was learning to train using only her kibble. Not only was it budget friendly and healthy but it also helped build a strong relationship between us. The Newton Cradle method was fantastic, so much fun and we saw real behavioural progress when applying it outdoors.

Although the course is fully online, I still received regular check-ins from Jacob and the YCA team and options for tailored support if I wanted to go further. After completing the challenge, I reached out to continue Koko’s training and I love that the next steps are fully personalised to her pace and needs.

I’d honestly recommend the Focus in Four Challenge to any dog owner (whether your dog is reactive or not). It lays solid groundwork, helps build a strong bond and gives you tools that genuinely make a difference. I’m just really grateful I took the leap. The Focus in Four Challenge gave us an incredible foundation, and it opened the door to ongoing support and training with an amazing team who genuinely care.

Copper and I have had our fair share of learning throughout our nearly three years together. The perspective I’ve consistently maintained throughout our journey is that I wouldn’t settle for a life of pure management, stress, avoidance, and fear— but more importantly I’ve also had an unwillingness to accept that things couldn’t get better.

Copper is a rescue that was adopted in his peak developmental fear period—who was nervy, lacked confidence, quite under-socialized, and horribly reactive from day one— I on the other hand, was a first time dog owner way out of my depth!

Fast forward; I digested everything I could (books and podcasts, gone to seminars, etc.) to find him still reactive and things increasingly getting worse. We’d been rushed and attacked by off lead dogs, developed a bite history, worked with six trainers (one of which was a board/train), improperly used tools and unintentionally enhanced feelings, made some progress with set backs— but ultimately we still fell short of seeing the results I knew were possible.

Enter, Yorkshire Canine Academy! 🌟🌟🌟At this point, I’ve quite literally moved to the other side of the globe and found it virtually impossible to find a trainer to work with in person. I am so grateful to have been “forced” to seek an online program and that the program I found was YCA. The structure of the program itself was easy to follow and the guidance along the way has been exceptional (timeline accommodates the owner’s motivation and life schedule, any previous training history, the dog’s characteristics/personality, and the owner’s end goal and more). Even having been a world apart and on a wildly different time zone— I still have felt heard, considered, and supported. The time/energy that the trainers have provided throughout the program as well as the individualized support has been what truly sets Training with Instinct at YCA apart.

While I shared that I always felt there had to be “more” for us— I genuinely never could have imagined a life with Copper anything like we have now. It’s hard to put into words how different our life is now because nearly every day I am blown away by how different of a dog he is— playful, relaxed, silly, sweet, TRUSTING, RESILIENT and so much more! I now have a dog that thinks on his feet and is present enough to make the right choices on his own— and if he is unsure, he seeks my guidance!

If you are at all on the fence about this program being the right fit, let me tell you from the bottom of my heart how much I wish that YCA had been the first trainer I started with— knowing how different Copper’s and my first few years would have been— unimaginable— but I suppose that journey is also what helped us get to where we are.

Simply put, if you’re an owner who wants more for your dog and your life together, and that is willing to put in the work to get there— you’ve found your place!

A word of warning…

We first contacted yca at the end of 2022. While we initially enjoyed the training and classes, over time we felt the environment was no longer right for us.
The obedience classes became repetitive, and I felt my dog was not progressing. I felt the environment was cliquey and that the trainers favoured certain dog breeds - which in my opinion should not be done in front of the clients.

I also had concerns about some handling methods, as I personally felt they were too firm for my dog at times, who began showing signs of stress. I was encouraged to just be “firmer” with her.

Additionally, we noticed social media posts from the business that, in our opinion were unprofessional and did not align with our values. As a result we chose to step away entirely.

Following this, I updated my review to reflect my honest experiences and evolving perspective on the business. In response, they claimed that my review was left because I was a “close friend of a competitor”. While I acknowledge that a friend of mine is a former employee or yca, this has absolutely nothing to do with my review or the intentions behind it. I believe this accusation is simply an attempt to discredit my review and suppress my honest feedback.

I have now received communication from yca claiming that my review is defamatory and they will proceed with legal action if I do not remove it within 48hrs.

I believe I am being unfairly targeted for simply sharing my genuine experience. I am also aware of others who have received similar emails regarding legal action following their reviews, which, in my opinion raises concerns about how this business handles customer feedback.

My review is an accurate and truthful account of my personal experience as a paying customer. It does not violate Google’s policies, nor does it meet the legal threshold for defamation. Attempting to suppress legitimate customer feedback through legal threats is deeply concerning and, in my opinion raises questions about how they handle criticism when it does not align with their preferred narrative.

During my time as a client, the business openly discussed offering free sessions in exchange for 5 star reviews, and I have proof of this. While I cannot speak about how reviews are handled now, I encourage potential customers to consider all 5 star reviews carefully and do their own research.

I stand by my review and my right to share my experience without fear of intimidation. Based on what I have encountered, I encourage anyone considering this business to research thoroughly and form their own judgment.

Before the YCA training, we’d refrain from taking Ziggy to pubs, cafes and got to a point where we didn’t want to let him off lead. We got our cockerpoo Ted last January and did textbook things wrong, over socialised him at day care and thought we’d achieved good boundaries by just crate training and putting in a baby gate to stop him going upstairs.

Gradually he become more and more reactive we’d read and heard various advice so tried coaxing him away from barking with the classics - cheese and by trying to be the most interesting thing to him which didn’t work. By February it had gotten so bad we couldn’t go out the front door for fear of seeing a dog, cat, car, person or even a tree moving in the wind would set him off!

Sometimes you have to hit rock bottom though as this was the kick we needed. We started back to basics with the Focus in Four building on his food drive ahead of our first 1 to 1 with Elisha.

Five weeks on and he’s a completely different dog! We’ve had 4 sessions and countless Q&As in our WhatsApp group (sorry Elisha 🤣). Ted is now e collar trained and apart from at a random hedgehog on tv had not reacted since!

Last Sunday we went to Roundhay park for the first time with him which is a reactive dog’s nightmare as there’s always dozens of dogs so a real test. He was off the lead perfect recall and choosing to come back to us when a dog came too close.  We are now fully confident walking him off lead in any setting.

I can’t believe how much it’s changed our lives and more importantly Ted’s life. Before he was always on edge and felt we’d let him down not having the tools & ability to help him live his best dog life!

We bumped into a neighbour recently who actually thought we’d re-homed him because they’d not heard him bark in a few weeks!

Looking forward to continuing his training and can actually plan day trips we never thought possible!

We wish we’d signed up sooner, so for anyone sitting on the fence contemplating, take the plunge.
We have a 2.5 year old Rottweiler, he was the most perfect puppy but like some males, adolescence hit and he became a total d**k. Which was really unfortunate as we loved our walks, taking him everywhere, and just giving him the best life possible. But life quickly became avoiding all dogs to avoid risk although he only had lead related issues with some dogs, stress free walks were in enclosed fields, and taking him everywhere was no longer an option planning walks/days out/staycations became a whole military operation and in certain circumstances impossible.

Our first stop wasn’t YCA unfortunately, we tried some advice which was full on aversion, which massively exaggerated issues and we discontinued it quickly. Our second stop was a local positive only dog trainer, and to give credit where credit is due, it built our boys confidence 10x…but it didn’t get down to the root of his reactivity. We still weren’t able to take him everywhere we wanted, when going out for walks we had pockets full of stuff and forgetting anything would be a knock to the confidence before we’d even started. Reactions were starting to become few and far between, but even more intense. We didn’t want to add to the Rottie stereotype, and we needed to nip his reactivity in the bud before it had the potential to put him in a dangerous situation.

We did all the research on YCA as you probably are now, we watched all the YouTube, listened to all the podcasts, and started to download all the freebies. We saw an immediate improvement with his engagement, but still we were eager to tackle his reactivity.

We booked in for our intro call with Chloe, she was accommodating, listened, asked all the right questions. And even politely challenged us, we were laser focused on his reactivity, but Chloe dug into his recall and asked us if he returns to us every time, which unless there’s a squeaky ball on offer, that would be a no, and you’re up s**t creek if he already had one.

We were then given access to the course content, and all the one-pagers and docs which help carry you through the course. The course layout has changed since we’ve been on the course, we’ve heard other members say it’s difficult to navigate but for us personally we had no issue. Although it’s recommended against to avoid overwhelming yourself or skipping critical steps, we spent a few days watching listening to every video beginning to end. But we rewatched and made notes for the stages we were at, at that current time. Which helps you contextualise and know where certain content is should you need it.

However you also have the daily check in calls, and the WhatsApp group with all the head trainers for help if you have any questions.

I’m sure much to the dismay of the team but we were regular contributors to the WhatsApp chat, with many a message/video, however the guys always made time to give us a message, voice note or video to help us on our journey. Kirky even messaged us back on Christmas Day. Kirky was also solid and straight to the point, when things didn’t go how we wanted them to and encouraged us to get straight back to training when we thought it was the end of the world.

We loved the remote training so much and our boy was doing so well, we made the 5-hour trip to visit YCA in person. We met Elisha, Jacob and Kirky. Everyone was welcoming, happy to give advice, just generally lovely people and you can tell they care about your dog.

Couldn’t recommend it more. We still have work to do to get him to where we want him to be. But it’s the best feeling to have our dog back, and there are certain behaviours which tell us he’s just happier. He was never a cuddly dog before, whereas now he loves a cuddle, this may be a coincidence but our relationship in general has improved majorly.

Thank you YCA Team! Can’t thank you enough. ❤️

I was personally at my wits end with Cassie, she was reactive to dogs to the extent that I could barely go out of the house, if we saw a dog she would go mad and it was completely heartbreaking, it was constant worrying that she would never be ok, not knowing what to do about it, months and months of obsessively watching every positive reinforcement dog training video, hours of reading everything online. It took over my life. We hired a local positive reinforcement trainer who was about as helpful as a chocolate fireguard. At this point the problem seemed unsolvable and I was an emotional wreck. About a day after we got her back I walked Cassie down the busiest dog walking street in Harrogate and she trotted past as if they weren’t even there!

However it is important to say, progress is not linear, Cassie completely regressed after a few weeks but it was because we as owners had not worked out how to be as consistent as Elisha, it’s been a huge learning curve and it takes a hell of a lot of strength and faith and commitment. She is not perfect, it’s constant training. right now her heel is terrible but she has stopped reacting to 95% of dogs.

ALSO - we used the e-collar on YCAs advice and only 3 months down the line we almost never have to use it, she has complete freedom off lead as recall is 100%.
